players.comment: James (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Nets. As expected, James won't play in the second half of Philly's back-to-back set after finishing Sunday's 131-124 victory over Indiana with 15 points (5-8 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), seven rebounds, 11 assists and one block across 33 minutes. The veteran superstar has yet to play in both halves of a back-to-back set this season, and that trend is unlikely to change. Dean Wade and Jabari Walker are candidates for increased roles in James' absence.

Smart has been suspended three games for throwing a punch during Wednesday's matchup against Golden State, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Smart, who was ejected from Wednesday's game for punching Charles Bassey, will begin serving his suspension Friday night against the Jazz, meaning he'll be eligible to return Wednesday versus Indiana. Bruce Thornton and Reed Sheppard should be in line for more minutes while Smart serves his three-game ban.

Adams (calf) is out for Monday's game against the Heat. The veteran big man is sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set. Tari Eason should see an uptick in playing time in the frontcourt for the Rockets on Monday.

LaVine is out for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City due to illness, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports. LaVine was ruled out shortly before tipoff after falling ill. Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk should be in line for additional opportunities Sunday with LaVine sidelined.

Capela (ankle) is out for Monday's game against the Heat. The veteran big man's next chance to return from an ankle sprain comes Wednesday in Indiana. Tari Eason should continue to see a bump in playing time in the frontcourt for the Rockets on Monday.

Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball. Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

Landale (hip) is out for Sunday's game against Bucks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. Landale missed four games earlier this month with a left hip issue, and he'll sit out Sunday due to right hip inflammation. Look for Zuby Ejiofor to see more minutes behind starter Onyeke Okongwu with Landale out of commission Sunday.

Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports. Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis. This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Brown (hamstring/head) will undergo further evaluation Tuesday and could receive an MRI, Kris Rhim of ESPN reports. Brown turned in a stellar performance with 31 points and 13 rebounds in Monday's win over Brooklyn, but he also dealt with left hamstring tightness and an apparent head issue that contributed to him sitting out the final 1:44 of regulation. The fact that the 30-year-old played through the ailments down the stretch could be an encouraging sign, though he'll undergo further evaluation Tuesday and an MRI is a possibility. Philadelphia's next game is Wednesday at Orlando, and if Brown is sidelined, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons could see an uptick in playing time.

DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports. DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics. Isaac's 2026-27 season debut will have to wait, as he's still working his way back from a left knee injury. He should be considered week-to-week until Orlando provides a clear update for his return.

Hunter (hip) is out for Sunday's game against the Thunder. Hunter was added to the injury report close to tipoff, and he's since been downgraded to out. The Kings will be forced to play shorthanded Sunday, as Precious Achiuwa (ankle) and Zach LaVine (illness) are also unavailable. The absence of three starters should open up minutes for Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp, Keegan Murray and Malik Monk.

Jerome (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Wizards. Jerome will miss a second straight matchup while nursing right hip soreness. Cam Spencer could receive another chance to start at point guard in Jerome's absence. The Virginia product's next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday in Cleveland.

Coach Erik Spoelstra stated after Monday's 128-110 win over Houston that the team held Adebayo (hip) out of the second half in an effort to be proactive, and the injury isn't expected to be a long-term issue, Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald reports. This is positive news for the star center, who didn't come out of the locker room to start the second half of Monday's clash. Miami will presumably re-evaluate Adebayo over the next few days to determine whether he'll be able to suit up for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee.

Merrill (elbow) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bulls. Merrill is set to miss his sixth consecutive game due to a right elbow injury. With the majority of the Cavs' starting lineup expected to return versus Chicago, Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas should continue to see the majority of Merrill's vacated minutes in the backcourt.

Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports. Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

players.comment: Nembhard (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Nembhard will miss his third contest of the season due to left hip soreness. T.J. McConnell should slide into the first unit while Quenton Jackson gets a boost in minutes off the bench.

Head coach Rick Carlisle said Wednesday that Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least 10 more days, Alex Golden of SI.com reports. Haliburton is still recovering from a left hamstring strain and will need more time to ramp up. Andrew Nembhard should continue seeing increased on-ball duties in Haliburton's stead, while Quenton Jackson and Braden Smith are also candidates for increased burn.

Williams (hamstring) will miss at least one week, per Anthony Slater of ESPN.com. Williams has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain in the aftermath of Monday's game against the Pelicans, and his status for Golden State's upcoming five-game road trip is in serious doubt. With Williams facing an extended absence, the Warriors are likely to lean more on De'Anthony Melton in the backourt.

Smith (undisclosed) exited in the fourth quarter of Monday's 126-115 loss to the Cavaliers and did not return. Smith collided with Peyton Watson at the rim, and both players stayed down several minutes before eventually leaving the contest. Smith did return to the bench after initially going back to the locker room, but Chicago opted to keep him out for good with the tilt in its final stages. He had a stellar outing prior to his exit, finishing with 17 points (6-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks in 28 minutes. The Bulls will provide an update on his health when available.

Queta (rest) won't play in Monday's game against the Magic, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports. The big man is sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set Monday, but he should be good to go for Wednesday's showdown in Denver. Mitchell Robinson is the most likely choice to replace Queta in the starting lineup, while Luka Garza should see a sizable chunk of the center minutes.

Murphy (knees) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Golden State. Murphy is set to miss a fifth consecutive game while he works his way back from bilateral patellar tendinopathy. His next chance to suit up will come against the Pistons on Wednesday. Saddiq Bey will likely remain in the starting unit for as long as Murphy is sidelined.
Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Golden State. Watford will miss a fifth consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. He remains without a clear return timetable.

Achiuwa (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports. Achiuwa is battling with ankle soreness and will miss a second straight game while on the mend. Keegan Murray drew the start in Achiuwa's absence Friday and is a good candidate to do so again Sunday evening.

Williams (finger) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's game against Cleveland. Williams suffered an injury to his right pinky finger that will end his night prematurely in Cleveland. The forward will finish with no points (0-2 FG, 0-1 3Pt) across 13 minutes of action. Noa Essengue figures to see an uptick in playing time should Williams miss extended time. Williams' next chance to suit up will come Wednesday at Brooklyn.

Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week. Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days. Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports. Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks. Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks. Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

Christie (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics. Christie will miss a second consecutive game due to sprained left ankle. With Kyrie Irving (knee) also out for Dallas, Naji Marshall, Zaccharie Risacher and Walter Clayton Jr. will help fill the vacated minutes in the backcourt.

Stewart is out for Monday's game against the Wizards due to an illness. The big man can be considered day-to-day ahead of Wednesday's meeting in Cleveland. A big workload could be in store for Zach Edey (ankle) if he's able to play for the Grizzlies on Monday.

Williams (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Kings. Williams will miss a sixth straight contest due to lower-back spasms and is still without a timetable to return. Isaiah Hartenstein, Kenrich Williams and rookie Aday Mara will continue holding down the frontcourt for as long as Williams is sidelined.

Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic. The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Kuminga (shoulder) exited in the fourth quarter of Monday's 106-98 win over Portland and did not return. He closed with 13 points (5-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), nine rebounds and one assist across 29 minutes. Kuminga put together a productive performance before aggravating his right shoulder on a shot attempt, exiting at the 6:35 mark of the fourth quarter and not returning. The forward's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday in a rematch against Portland, though the quick turnaround makes his availability highly questionable pending further updates. Should Kuminga miss time, Terrence Shannon could see an increased workload.

Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports. This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Warriors. McGowens will miss a third consecutive outing due to an infection in his left elbow. Jaron Pierre Jr. will continue earning extra minutes off the Pelicans' bench with McGowens and Bennedict Mathurin (foot) both sidelined.

Watson left Monday's 126-115 win over Chicago due to a head injury and did not return. As expected, Watson missed the remainder of Cleveland's victory after taking a nasty fall on a drive to the basket with a little more than five minutes left in the game. He recorded 14 points (5-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds and one blocks across 22 minutes. We'll know more once the Cavs provide an update on Watson's status moving forward.

Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Rollins (illness) is out for Sunday's game against the Hawks. Rollins will miss his first game of the season due to an illness. Gary Trent, AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis are candidates for increased roles with Rollins sidelined.

Aldama (ankle) is out for Sunday's game against the Celtics. Aldama will miss Sunday's game with an ankle injury, which is not surprising given it is the second half of a back-to-back set. Morez Johnson could see extra minutes with Aldama out.

Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports. Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced. Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

Larsson won't play in Monday's game against the Rockets due to an illness, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Larsson, who came down with an illness last week, is a spectator for a third consecutive contest Monday. His continued absence should create another start for Myron Gardner and more playing time for Andrew Wiggins off the bench.

The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL. Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Warriors. Mathurin will miss a second straight game and his third over the last four outings due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot. Jordan Poole and Jaron Pierre Jr. will continue to get extended run with Mathurin on the shelf.

Lively (foot) is listed as out for Thursday's game in Minnesota. Lively is still working his way back from foot surgery. He's reportedly trending favorably, though he should continue to be classified as week-to-week, at least until the team provides an update. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford is expected to stay in the starting lineup, with Morez Johnson (shin), Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse all in line to spend time at the five when needed.

Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports. Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

Tyson (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Chicago. Tyson was downgraded to doubtful earlier in the day, and the team has since reported that he'll be held out of Monday's action due to right ankle injury management. Look for Meleek Thomas, Tyrese Proctor and Tristan Enaruna to see more run in Tyson's absence.

Thompson (knee) is out for Monday's game against the Heat. The star guard is missing the back end of this back-to-back set Monday and is likely facing a short-term absence. Reed Sheppard stands out as a strong streaming option for fantasy managers Monday.

Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

Youngblood (foot) is out for Monday's game against the Timberwolves. Youngblood will miss a third straight game due to a right foot bone bruise. His next opportunity to suit up comes Tuesday against the Timberwolves.

Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

Barlow (back) will be re-evaluated later in the week and is thought to be nearing his 2026-27 season debut, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports. Barlow has yet to take the court this season due to a back injury, but he's trending in the right direction. He was spotted participating in shootaround Thursday, and if all goes well during his re-evaluation, the team could have additional news on when he'll make his season debut.

Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

Newell (toe) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Chicago. Newell will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left great toe hyperextension. He can be considered week-to-week until the Hawks provide an update on his progress.

Raynaud (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder. Raynaud will miss his 13th consecutive game to start 2026-27 after injuring his knee during the preseason. It sounds like the Frenchman is getting closer to making his season debut, with his next chance to do so coming Wednesday versus Phoenix.

Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN. It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports. Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

Jovic (illness) is out for Monday's game against Houston. Jovic was added to the injury report as questionable due to an illness earlier in the day Monday, and the club has since determined that he won't be able to give it a go. Klay Thompson and Bobby Portis could pick up a few additional minutes in Jovic's absence, though the impact to Miami's rotation should be minimal.

Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Memphis. Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards offer an update on his progress.

Sorber (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers. Sorber is still recovering from knee surgery and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Thunder offer an update on his status.

Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

Jackson will undergo surgery to repair the broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot and is set to miss significant time. The Grizzlies will release a timeline for Jackson's return to basketball activities after he undergoes surgery, though he's facing a lengthy absence. With the 22-year-old forward on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant are candidates for increased playing time.

Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Cavaliers. Awaka will miss a fourth consecutive game due a disc irritation in his back. His next chance to suit up will come against the Nets on Wednesday.

Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday. Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports. The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

Tomlin is set to miss several weeks with a lower back stress reaction, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. This is a tough blow for the forward and there's no guarantee he's cleared right away when he's re-evaluated in three-to-four weeks. Tomlin wasn't projected to crack the rotation ahead of Opening Night and was penciled in to be an emergency depth option.

Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com. With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.
Biberovic (heel) is out for Thursday's game against Minnesota. Biberovic remains plagued by right heel bursitis. The rookie forward carries no timetable for his season debut.

Flemings (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bucks. Flemings left Friday's 125-117 loss to Chicago with back tightness after playing 17 minutes. The ailment will keep the rookie first-rounder on the sidelines Sunday, with veteran CJ McCollum the likely candidate to join the starting lineup. Flemings' next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus Oklahoma City.

Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com. The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

De Larrea (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game at Minnesota. De Larrea hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a right knee sprain, but he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Still, he can be considered week-to-week until Dallas provides an update on his progress.

Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics. Irving was listed as questionable to face Boston after playing 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss in Cleveland.
